data.title: U.S. Appeals Court Upholds Pentagon Labeling Anthropic a Security Risk — WSJ
data.description:
By Amrith Ramkumar and Heather Somerville

WASHINGTON-A federal appeals court upheld the Defense Department's decision to designate Anthropic a security risk, giving the Trump administration a win in its complicated feud with one of the nation's top artificial-intelligence developers.

The federal appeals court in Washington said in a 2-1 decision Friday that the law giving the Pentagon the authority to deem a company a supply-chain risk gave Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth the latitude to take the action against Anthropic because the company's refusal to have its AI tools used in mass surveillance or autonomous weapons could undermine military operations.

"The Department had ample support for its conclusion that the continued integration of Claude into the Department's information systems, by the Department or its contractors, presented a statutorily covered national-security risk," the court wrote. Anthropic had argued that the designation was an unprecedented attack retaliating against the company for disagreeing with the Defense Department in contract negotiations. A federal judge in California recently sided with the company in a parallel dispute covering parts of the designation under a different statute, fueling uncertainty about the future of the supply-chain risk label.

Legal analysts have said that a split between the courts could ultimately lead to the Supreme Court.

"We respectfully disagree with the court's decision. Another federal court has already held the government's parallel designation unlawful. We remain confident in our position and are considering all options, including further review," an Anthropic spokeswoman said.

The supply-chain risk is normally used on companies based in foreign adversaries like China's Huawei who pose security risks. AI analysts have said the administration's move was a self-inflicted wound in the global AI race because it could damage Anthropic, which makes some of the nation's most powerful models and has said it has lost contracts and suffered reputational harm from the move.

A win for the government could give the Pentagon more latitude to take similar actions against companies in the future, analysts have said.

The rulings are part of a delicate relationship between the Trump administration and Anthropic, which are working together on the release of new AI models while the legal fight continues. The company has vaulted ahead in the AI race by many measures and is barreling toward an initial public offering in which it is aiming for a valuation of about $2 trillion.

Pentagon officials have said the department is nearly entirely done moving away from Anthropic's models using tools from OpenAI and other competitors.

At a hearing at the federal appeals court earlier this year, the three-judge panel appeared split, with two of the judges seeming sympathetic to the administration's argument that it had the authority to use the supply-chain risk designation regardless of the guardrails Anthropic was pursuing in their negotiations.

"It's about risk, and they say, 'Well, based on what we know, we can't trust that the [AI] model may not have something embedded within it that is going to create a problem for military capabilities," said Neomi Rao, a judge appointed during the first Trump administration.

Judge Karen LeCraft Henderson, who was appointed by former President George H.W. Bush, disagreed and published a dissenting opinion Thursday. "To me this is just a spectacular overreach by the department," she said during the hearing.

Write to Amrith Ramkumar at amrith.ramkumar@wsj.com and Heather Somerville at heather.somerville@wsj.com

data.title: Edelweiss Financial Services sells 45% Nido Home Finance stake to Carlyle for ₹600 crore
data.description:
Edelweiss Financial Services Ltd on Friday (September 25) announced the completion of Carlyle’s investment of over ₹2,000 crore in Nido Home Finance Ltd, giving the global investment firm’s affiliated funds a strategic majority stake in the housing finance company.

The investment funds affiliated with Carlyle Asia Partners (CAP), part of The Carlyle Group, have invested approximately ₹2,000 crore, or about $215 million, in Nido through a combination of primary capital infusion and secondary purchase.

The primary capital infusion is approximately ₹1,450 crore, of which around ₹725 crore has been received. The balance is to be received within 18 months. Following the primary infusion, Nido’s net worth is set to nearly triple to approximately ₹2,300 crore within 18 months.

Carlyle has also completed the secondary purchase of a 45% stake in Nido from Edelweiss for approximately ₹600 crore. Edelweiss will hold approximately 26% of Nido on a fully diluted basis at the end of 18 months.

Edelweiss will also receive a share of the upside if Carlyle realises returns above a specified threshold. The transaction was announced on February 10, 2026, and has been completed following receipt of the requisite regulatory and statutory approvals.

Nido, established in 2010, is a housing finance company offering home loan solutions across the affordable housing and mid-ticket market segments. Its branch network serves more than 800 talukas, or sub-districts, and it had assets under management of ₹4,900 crore as of the quarter ended June 2026.

For Edelweiss, the transaction provides Nido with fresh growth capital, while allowing Edelweiss to monetise part of its stake and reduce debt. Nido will also have access to Carlyle’s operating expertise.

The company said the primary equity infusion is expected to strengthen Nido’s financial foundation and position it to serve affordable and mid-ticket housing segments across rural, semi-urban and emerging markets.

Edelweiss operates seven independent businesses spanning alternative asset management, mutual funds, asset reconstruction, non-banking finance, housing finance, general insurance and life insurance. It employs more than 6,000 people, serves around 1.4 crore customers and manages around ₹2,80,000 crore of assets.

Shares of Edelweiss Financial Services Ltd ended at ₹137.20, down by ₹1.85, or 1.33%, on the BSE.

data.title: 'Lift Your Game': Former Australian PM Kevin Rudd Addresses OpenAI CEO Over Portal Breach — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Andy Serwer

Kevin Rudd, the former prime minister of Australia, has something to say to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman-and the rest of Silicon Valley.

"Lift your game, Sam," Rudd said Thursday in an interview with me at Journal House, which was held on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

Rudd was speaking about an incident this summer in which an OpenAI agent infiltrated a government-services website in Australia. The breach was disclosed by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on Wednesday at the United Nations meeting in New York.

"I'm just being very blunt about it," said Rudd. "There's sometimes a bit of a cavalier culture out there in [Silicon] Valley about these things. We're a sovereign state. We take our cyber defenses seriously. We're a modern democracy. We have an excellent collaborative relationship with the major AI companies and the platform providers, but it does depend on them notifying us when a problem arises."

The Wall Street Journal reported that that the OpenAI incident appears to be the first publicly disclosed occurence of an artificial-intelligence agent gaining unauthorized access to a government service. Albanese said the incident began June 18, and that the agent gained access to both public and nonpublic files in the country's public-facing healthcare statistics portal, which reports spending and other information.

OpenAI confirmed the incident, with a spokesperson telling The Journal, "In the course of that, our models took actions we did not intend."

The incident occurred in June, but OpenAI did not discover it until August and reported it to the Australians on Sept. 10th, the Journal reported. Rudd, the former ambassador to the United States and current CEO of the educational non-profit Asia Society, thinks OpenAI did a poor job of notifying the Australian government about the problem.

"OpenAI apparently had their own internal awareness of this some time ago, but there was a huge delay in their formal notification of the Australian government," he said. "OpenAI is saying they sent some obscure email to some obscure inbox somewhere. The bottom line is, if you've got an AI agent, which you know as the originating company has breached cyber defenses of the social or economic infrastructure of one of your partner countries in a large market, then you should be on the telephone immediately, so that the appropriate agencies, in our case the Australian Signals Directorate, can automatically act on cyber defenses through our own cyber command."

OpenAI did not immediately respond to Barron's request for comment.

I asked Rudd what sort of damage the breach caused.

"I'm sure the [Prime Minister] will outline later to the Australian people what, if anything, was compromised," Rudd said. "Now, I'm not in that loop-I've now left government service about three months ago. But we take these things step by step."

"Look, mistakes happen," he added. "We understand that nothing in the world is perfect, but given how fast this game is moving in terms of frontier models, not withstanding what [Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei] had to say the other day, this now needs to be a much smoother operation than is currently the case in terms of the intersection between the frontier model-has it been tested against cyber defenses before its release? If not-and even if so, and if a breach occurs, to immediately get on the phone to say, 'Houston, we have a problem,' or 'Sydney, we have a problem.'"

Write to Andy Serwer at andy.serwer@barrons.com

data.title: What's Moving Markets Today? — WSJ
data.description:
By Shradha Dinesh

Major stock indexes ticked up on Friday following a dizzying news week spanning record high yields on Treasurys, seesawing updates on the state of negotiations with Iran, a Chinese state visit and more.

Here's what is moving markets today:

Oil prices: After remaining quiet for much of the morning, Brent crude extended declines after initial reports suggest that sideline talks between the U.S. and Iran from the U.N. assembly in New York have progressed to a "technical stage," according to Al-Jazeera. Brent crude fell about 3% to $97 a barrel.

Tech: Five of the Magnificent Seven are up. Meta Platforms and Tesla are, so far, Friday's laggards. Meta rode the wave of enthusiasm for its new personal AI agent, Muse, and followed up with its expansions into hardware Wednesday. The company unveiled a handheld keychain device that can be used to talk to Muse agents and added Muse to its more controversial smartglasses.

Diesel: The nationwide average diesel price per gallon, which hit a record-breaking $6.53 Tuesday, has ended its daily new-record streak. Prices in the back half of the week have hovered around $6.50, according to AAA. The slowdown follows a week of public back-and-forth as some candidates facing tight midterm races said they would back a diesel export ban.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Trump Calls Xi Meeting 'Very Productive.' What Investors Might Not Like. — Barrons.com
data.description:
Reshma Kapadia

President Donald Trump said in a social media post Friday he had a "very productive" meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, but offered few details.

Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a television interview Friday that details of what the two sides reached on trade would come Monday.

While investors likely will be pleased to see signs of a fragile peace between the two economic superpowers and indications that the leaders could meet at least twice more this year, the lack of deals and a shorter-than-expected extension of the rivals' latest truce leaves plenty of uncertainty for markets in the months ahead.

In fact, the biggest takeaway for investors so far actually happened before the summit. The two countries extended their truce that was set to expire on Nov. 10 for another two months-the brief extension underscores the distrust and frictions simmering beneath the friendly tone that the leaders struck.

"I had been pretty sanguine on the U.S.-China relationship. But with an extension of only two months, that's a bit concerning," says Rory Green, head of China research for TS Lombard.

Greer told CNBC on Friday that the two sides had made fresh progress in negotiations around U.S. agricultural products, medical devices, and Chinese consumer goods deemed nonsensitive, with more information coming next week. The U.S. and China have been discussing a Board of Trade that would lower tariffs on $30 billion of nonstrategic goods, with analysts expecting many of them to be consumer-oriented.

Otherwise, the much-anticipated summit between the leaders of the world's two largest economies brought a lot of optics, but not much substance. Xi's first visit to Washington, D.C. in a decade was heavy on ceremony and goodwill-building: Trump greeted him on the tarmac in a rare move, hosted him for a state dinner, and said they have "never gotten along better." Xi has been pushing to be recognized as a global power on par with the U.S., something the visit reinforced.

Both leaders talked up their strong rapport and vowed increased cooperation and communication as they try to navigate their geopolitical rivalry. Trump and Xi are intent on preserving stability to buy each country time to reduce their dependence on the other-and to forestall a series of retaliatory measures that would make both economies' domestic problems worse.

China's economy is still stuck in a multiyear rout, with another batch of data showing weakness, even as Xi tries to project strength and equal standing with the U.S. on the global stage. Trump has his own problems, including the Iran war stretching into its seventh month and rising prices ahead of midterm elections.

The talks, however, did little to address the biggest issues among the rivals. Among them are China's support for Iran and increased military posture in Asia, the continued trade imbalance between the U.S. and China, and the two countries' race to develop artificial intelligence. Instead, the short truce extension underscores U.S. concerns about its access to rare-earth minerals and a desire to keep China to its commitments.

The U.S. is focused on getting rare-earth flows back to levels before the flare-up with China last summer, but exports are still down 25%, according to Scott Kennedy, a senior adviser at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

That gives China some leverage: The country could clamp down on those rare earths used in everything from autos to semiconductors.

That means if the U.S.-China relationship's precarious stability wavers, investors may need to brace again for higher costs, whether they result from tariffs, shortages, or supply chain disruptions.

Brian McCarthy, managing partner at Macrolens, sees the short extension as a signal that escalation could follow, particularly because there have been few signs of progress on the administration's goal of rebalancing the relationship.

"A number of U.S. officials anticipate that the U.S.-China relationship will likely encounter some turbulent waters in the weeks after the visit, even as we expect these other leader-level meetings to continue to provide a veneer of stability," says Daniel Kritenbrink, a former diplomat and now partner at consultancy The Asia Group.

Potential irritants loom, including the Trump administration's Section 301 investigation into excess capacity that could result in tariffs of 7.5% or more against China, as well as a spate of Congressional efforts to tighten restrictions on China.

The two sides also said they would begin a dialogue over AI safety. However, there were few details and little sign that AI experts from either side were in the room-leaving investors unnerved that tensions over AI are only going to intensify.

"If U.S. tech firms agree to slow the pace of AI development domestically, it will increase calls in Washington for the U.S. to slow down China as well-such as by closing loopholes on Chinese AI firms' access to compute through the cloud," writes Michael Hirson, 22V Research's head of China research. "This raises the prospect of Chinese retaliation and is one reason why we continue to expect 2027 to see an increase in tensions around tech and supply chains."

Write to Reshma Kapadia at reshma.kapadia@barrons.com

data.title: Corporate debt maturities set to test US borrowers as rates rise
data.description:
By Patturaja Murugaboopathy

A growing wall of US corporate debt is set to mature from 2027, putting pressure on companies to refinance borrowings raised at ultra-low interest rates during the pandemic.

About $4.3 trillion of non-financial corporate bonds issued in US markets will mature between 2027 and 2031, a Reuters analysis of LSEG data showed. Annual maturities rise from about $572 billion in 2027 to roughly $1.03 trillion in 2030, after many companies pushed debt into later years through refinancing.

The challenge comes as global debt has climbed above a record $365 trillion, according to the Institute of International Finance, while higher Treasury yields have lifted refinancing costs across markets. The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield is above 5%, around its highest level since 2007.

As the debt comes due, companies that locked in cheap fixed-rate funding earlier in the decade will increasingly have to refinance at higher costs, pressuring earnings and cash flow.

The burden will be heaviest for lower-rated borrowers. High-yield bond maturities jump from about $68.5 billion in 2027 to $314.1 billion in 2029, according to LSEG, while investment-grade maturities increase to $512.6 billion from $437 billion.

High-yield debt will account for about a third of all maturities in 2029, up from 12% in 2027.

Bond fund manager PIMCO said most investment-grade and high-yield issuers should be able to absorb higher refinancing costs, but the weakest borrowers face a sharper squeeze. Coupons on CCC-rated bonds due in 2027 and 2028 could roughly double if refinanced at current index yields, it said.

The refinancing wave will coincide with heavy borrowing by major technology companies to fund artificial intelligence infrastructure. Goldman Sachs expects gross debt issuance by hyperscalers including Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle to reach $420 billion in 2027, up 60% from estimated 2026 levels.

data.title: SMX Digital Platform Makes Plastic a Passport and a Tradeable Asset
data.description:
NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / September 25, 2026 / SMX is taking its plastics technology beyond authentication, expanding its Digital Material Passport platform into an infrastructure that connects physical materials to the digital blockchain and, ultimately, to new markets for verified material assets.

The evolution represents a significant step beyond the passport itself. SMX's technology was designed to give plastic a persistent identity in the physical world, using molecular markers to authenticate what a material is, where it came from and how it moves through its lifecycle. The expanded platform now carries that identity into the digital world, creating a blockchain-linked record that can follow the material into verified markets, real-world asset applications and circularity credits.

In effect, SMX is building a bridge between physical material and digital value. A piece of plastic no longer has to exist only as an anonymous commodity whose history disappears as it moves through a supply chain. Its physical identity can be authenticated, translated into a Digital Material Passport and connected to a digital ecosystem where its provenance, composition and lifecycle become verifiable data with potential commercial value.

The expanded model creates a continuous progression:

Material → Passport → Blockchain → Market → Credit

SMX is also opening a new client experience around the platform, allowing companies to bring their own plastic into the process and test how it can be marked, identified, authenticated and connected to a Digital Material Passport. The experience is intended to demonstrate the complete system rather than an isolated technology, from the first molecular marker through verification, blockchain connectivity, lifecycle tracking and potential commercial applications.

At the first layer is SMX's molecular marking technology, which gives plastic a persistent physical identity. Invisible molecular markers are embedded directly into the material, allowing it to be authenticated later rather than relying exclusively on labels, certificates, invoices or supplier declarations.

The second layer is the Digital Material Passport Platform (DMPP), launched by SMX earlier this year. The DMPP connects that physical identity to a secure digital record containing information including origin, composition, chain of custody, recycled content, manufacturing history and lifecycle status.

The platform includes interactive dashboards for visibility across operations, blockchain-backed transaction timelines, data export capabilities, integrated management of compliance and audit documents, and lifecycle mapping from raw material through finished product and subsequent reuse cycles. Its modular, API-driven architecture is designed to integrate with existing enterprise and ERP systems.

That is an important distinction in the rapidly developing Digital Product Passport market. SMX is not simply creating a digital record about a material. Its system is designed to connect the record back to an identifier embedded in the physical material itself.

The next layer is Market.

Once the identity, composition, provenance and recycled content of plastic can be verified and carried into a blockchain-backed digital record, SMX's infrastructure is designed to allow that authenticated material to participate in digital and real-world asset markets. Instead of trading plastic based primarily on documentation and representations, buyers and sellers can potentially transact material carrying verifiable information about what it actually is.

The final layer is Credit, connecting verified recycling and reuse to SMX's circularity infrastructure.

Through its Circularity-as-a-Service platform, SMX is building the ability to document and certify plastic as it moves through recovery and reuse. Verified circularity events can then provide the underlying evidence for Plastic Circularity Credits, creating a potential economic value for an activity that historically has been difficult to prove consistently.

Together, the layers create a continuous chain:

The material is marked. The passport records it. The blockchain carries its identity into the digital world. The market recognizes it. The credit captures verified circularity.

ONE PLATFORM, MULTIPLE COMMERCIAL FUNCTIONS

The significance of the new client experience is that companies can now see those functions operating as parts of the same infrastructure.

A manufacturer could mark plastic at production and connect it to a Digital Material Passport. A converter or brand could authenticate its composition and origin. A recycler could verify the same material when it returns through a recovery stream. Its recycled content and lifecycle could remain associated with the material as it enters another production cycle.

The resulting verified data can support compliance and certification, but SMX is designing the infrastructure to go further: into material trading, real-world asset digitization and circularity credits.

That broader commercial capability is particularly relevant as recycled and virgin plastic enter what SMX calls the Age of Parity. War, oil and energy volatility, inflation, tariffs, petrochemical disruption, transportation costs and supply-chain pressure have changed the traditional economics of virgin plastic. At the same time, recycled-content mandates, plastic taxes and other regulatory pressures are increasing the economic importance of recovered material.

The result is a market in which recycled plastic can increasingly compete with virgin material on economics, not simply environmental preference.

And when recycled plastic has greater economic value, proving that it is actually recycled becomes considerably more important.

That is the problem SMX's platform is built to address.

The company is effectively connecting two markets that have traditionally operated separately: the physical plastics economy and the digital economy built around data, verification and increasingly tokenized real-world assets.

A ton of recycled plastic is still a ton of recycled plastic. But when its identity, composition, provenance, chain of custody and recycling history can be independently authenticated and carried with it into the digital world, it becomes a materially different commercial proposition.

COMPANIES CAN NOW PUT THEIR OWN PLASTIC THROUGH THE SYSTEM

SMX's new client experience is designed to make that proposition tangible.

Companies participating in the program can provide their own plastic material and experience how SMX molecularly marks it, authenticates it and connects it to the Digital Material Passport infrastructure.

That gives polymer producers, packaging companies, manufacturers, brands, recyclers and other participants in the plastics economy an opportunity to evaluate the technology using material from their own operations rather than through a generic demonstration.

The trial also provides a practical view of the larger SMX architecture: how physical verification feeds a digital passport, how that passport carries authenticated material identity onto the blockchain, how that digital identity can support verified material markets and how verified lifecycle events can ultimately support circularity credits.

It is the difference between being shown a platform and putting your own material through it.

ABOUT SMX (SECURITY MATTERS) PLC

SMX (Security Matters) PLC develops molecular traceability and material authentication technologies designed to strengthen supply-chain transparency and integrity across global industries. Its platform embeds invisible molecular markers directly into physical materials-including solids, liquids, and gases-allowing them to carry a persistent identity that can be detected and verified throughout their lifecycle.

SOURCE: SMX (Security Matters) Public Limited

data.title: Indian stock market slides, but 28 Nifty 500 stocks hit fresh 1-year highs this week; MCX, PVR Inox among them
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 25 -- Welspun Corp, Zydus Lifesciences, Engineers India, and Indegene were among over two dozen Nifty 500 stocks that hit fresh 1-year highs this week, even as the sell-off in the Indian stock market deepened.

These stocks, spanning from healthcare to financials, have defied the market weakness to reach fresh milestones as investors appeared to adopt selective buying, given the current market conditions, which are being dominated by elevated crude oil prices and surging global bond yields.

Nifty 50 finished the last week with a cut of 0.88%, extending its weekly losing streak to seven. This was the index's biggest sustained decline since 2020. It had recorded seven-week losing streaks only four times in the last 25 years.

Barring 2020, the index logged a seven-week decline in 2008 and twice in 2021, and in the same year, it registered one of its longest losing runs after falling for nine consecutive weeks.

Crude oil prices have been a focal point for markets since late February, when the US and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran, triggering a war in the Middle East.

According to Trendlyne data, Welspun Corp, Zydus Lifesciences, Engineers India, Indegene, Multi Commodity Exchange, and Allied Blenders & Distillers have registered their fresh one-year peaks in today's trade, 25 September.

While in Thursday's trade, pharma stocks such as Divi's Laboratories, Aurobindo Pharma, Laurus Labs, and Caplin Point Laboratories, along with Shyam Metalics and Energy and Carborundum Universal, rose to 52-week highs.

Other stocks such as Apollo Hospitals, Redington, RBL Bank, Welspun Living, Vijaya Diagnostic Centre, IDFC First Bank, Inventurus Knowledge Solutions, JSW Infrastructure, Tega Industries, Syrma SGS Technology, ACME Solar Holdings, Apar Industries, Action Construction, Usha Martin, Jyoti CNC Automation, and PVR Inox also touched fresh one-year highs.

Notably, Apollo Hospitals was the only stock from the Nifty 50 index to reach this level, while other index constituents such as Adani Ports & SEZ, JSW Steel, Titan Company, and Grasim Industries were also in the visible range of between 6% and 7%.

Looking ahead, domestic activity and global macro data will remain key market drivers. Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments, said domestic IIP data will test the durability of industrial activity, while US job openings, GDP, the core PCE deflator, and PMI readings, alongside commentary from Federal Reserve officials, will frame expectations on the rate path and global liquidity.

"With crude hostage to geopolitics and yields elevated, valuation expansion looks constrained, leaving earnings delivery as the principal driver of returns. The strength in domestic activity signalled by the PMI, alongside steady domestic liquidity, should limit the downside, though investors would be prudent to stay selective and favor earnings visibility and valuation comfort," he further added.

data.title: UBS hires Financial Advisors John Pham and Jimmy Yip in Silicon Valley
data.description:
UBS today announced that Financial Advisors John Pham and Jimmy Yip have joined the firm’s offices in Palo Alto and San Jose, California. The team joins UBS from Merrill Lynch and will be part of the UBS San Francisco Market, led by Market Executive Emily de la Reguera and reports to Silicon Valley Market Director Jacqueline Kehoe.

“We are thrilled to welcome John, Jimmy, and their team to UBS,” said Emily de la Reguera. “John and Jimmy have built an exceptional team grounded in thoughtful advice, deep relationships and an unwavering commitment to their clients. Their experience serving the unique needs of Silicon Valley executives, entrepreneurs and families, together with the strength of our global wealth management platform, makes them an outstanding addition to UBS and an important part of our continued growth in the region.”

Market Director Jacqueline Kehoe worked closely with this team during her tenure at Merrill Lynch. The strong relationships and trust she developed with the team were instrumental in their decision to join UBS. “I have had the opportunity to work alongside this team and witness firsthand their dedication to delivering outstanding client service and fostering long-term relationships,“ said Jacqueline.

John Pham brings more than 22 years of experience advising Silicon Valley executives, entrepreneurs and families. He is known for his thoughtful approach to wealth management and his commitment to building lasting client relationships. His practice is centered on understanding each client’s complete financial picture and developing personalized strategies aligned with their long-term goals.

Jimmy Yip brings extensive financial services experience and a goals-based approach to advising working professionals, business owners and their families. He focuses on understanding each client’s goals, concerns and aspirations and developing tailored investment and wealth management strategies. Jimmy has worked in the financial services industry since 2004 and earned a bachelor’s degree in business marketing from San Jose State University.

John and Jimmy are joined by Client Associates Leslie Vinoya, Kimberly Russell and Randall Bane, who bring deep experience and a shared commitment to delivering exceptional client service.

Notes to Editors

UBS is a leading and truly global wealth manager and the leading universal bank in Switzerland. It also provides diversified asset management solutions and focused investment banking capabilities. UBS manages 7.3 trillion dollars of invested assets as per the second quarter 2026. UBS helps clients achieve their financial goals through personalized advice, solutions and products. data.title: Nymex Overview: Crude Futures Fall on US-Iran Diplomacy, Supply Risks — OPIS
data.description:
Oil futures fell midday Friday amid renewed diplomatic efforts to reach a U.S.-Iran agreement over the Strait of Hormuz, while continued threats to the Middle East energy infrastructure kept supply concerns in focus.

As of 12:35 p.m. ET, November ICE Brent crude was trading $3.06 lower at $103.54, with December down $3.50 at $96.72/bbl. The November West Texas Intermediate contract was trading $2.63 lower at $91.98/bbl, with December down $2.80 at $88.10/bbl.

Refined product futures were also falling. October RBOB traded 18.5cts lower at $3.3796/gal, with November down 15.04cts at $3.1904/gal. The October ULSD contract traded 14.41cts lower at $4.5862/gal, with November down 9.66cts at $4.4314/gal.

Diplomatic efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz face obstacles. Qatar and other mediators are seeking a new round of talks in Oman as soon as next week, according to The Wall Street Journal, while Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are urging Washington to maintain economic pressure on Iran and avoid concessions that would ease sanctions or the U.S. naval blockade.

The prospect of de-escalation is being weighed against continued threats to regional energy infrastructure. France plans to deploy soldiers, radar and defense systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect a refinery and crude-oil pipeline at the Red Sea port of Yanbu.

Near-term physical supply remains tight despite efforts to restore regional flows. Brent's front-month spread remained around $4 to $5/bbl, compared with less than $1/bbl in February, reflecting tight prompt supplies. The International Energy Agency said global observed oil inventories have fallen by 507 million bbl since the conflict began, including a 95 million-bbl draw in August.

Friday's decline follows a sharp rally Thursday, when Brent gained 3.4% and WTI rose 2.7% after Saudi Arabia reported intercepting missiles launched at the kingdom.

data.title: EU wheat eases again as Black Sea truce efforts assessed
data.description:
Euronext wheat fell on Friday to a one-month low as diplomatic initiatives raised hopes for a recovery in war-disrupted Black Sea exports, though continued attacks by Russia and Ukraine helped underpin prices, traders said.

Benchmark December milling wheat on Paris-based Euronext settled down 0.3% at €236.75 ($269.73) a metric ton after the day session.

The contract earlier dropped to €233.75, its lowest since August 25, with a chart gap created during an opening fall adding to selling momentum. But it later recovered to fill the gap and trade only slightly lower.

A slide in Chicago wheat , which fell around 3% before paring losses, pressured Euronext.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Friday the United States had proposed a trilateral meeting with Ukraine and Russia to discuss efforts to end the conflict, while the Kremlin said a trilateral meeting could happen soon.

Turkey, meanwhile, is pursuing efforts to broker a Black Sea truce.

Large long positions held by investors and careful buying by wheat importers have also encouraged the market off multi-year highs struck in early September.

"The market has been selling off with longs who are tired and consumers who will wait," a futures trader said.

Russia could quickly restart up to 80% of its grain terminal capacity in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov if diplomatic efforts result in a ceasefire, a Reuters analysis of industry data showed on Friday.

Continuing attacks by Russia and Ukraine, however, have tempered expectations of near-term de-escalation.

Grain markets also drew support from comments by US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, who said Washington expected to release on Monday details on the outcome of trade negotiations with China.

That offset initial disappointment over the absence of news on agricultural trade during a US-China summit this week.

In France, a vessel is loading a first shipment of wheat for Yemen in years, LSEG data showed, as Black Sea disruption generates some unusual demand for French wheat.

French traders are watching to see if rain forecast for the week ahead materialises ahead of cereal planting and after record drought reduced rapeseed sowing.

data.title: NexTel Medical Corp. Showcases Pioneer Exosome Technologies and Diagnostic Innovations at Leading Healthcare Conference
data.description:
Company highlights ongoing clinical developments in traumatic brain injury (TBI) therapeutics and non-invasive cancer screening, sparking key vendor collaboration discussions.

ORLANDO, FL / ACCESS Newswire / September 25, 2026 / NexTel Medical Corp. (f/k/a Exousia Pro, Inc.) , a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering proprietary exosome-based delivery and diagnostic systems, today announced the successful participation of its executive and medical leadership teams at this week's Orlando Health Conference.

Throughout the event, NexTel executives and key scientific advisors engaged directly with industry founders, medical device distributors, and commercial sales representatives to present the company's expanding platform technologies.

Key scientific highlights from the conference include:

  • Scientific Presentations: Dr. Sugaya delivered a comprehensive, three-hour briefing detailing NexTel's core pipeline developments. Additionally, Dr. Hausman conducted a virtual presentation from California focused on Maxasome™ PLUS and its therapeutic applications for Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI). Dr. Hausman is currently preparing a white paper exploring the application of mushroom-derived exosomes in treating TBI.
  • Strategic Executive Presence: NexTel's Head of Operations and Chief Executive Officer represented the company on-site throughout the week to drive high-level business development and strategic networking.
  • Commercialization & Educational Initiatives: Based on feedback gathered from market representatives, NexTel is updating its clinical and consumer educational materials to streamline product messaging. The company is actively producing a series of video tutorials demonstrating how its liquid biopsy cancer screening platform detects early-stage biomarkers in saliva, alongside educational modules outlining the therapeutic scope of Maxasome™ PLUS.

"Our strong presence at this week's conference underscored the immense market potential for our exosome delivery and diagnostic platforms," said Mathew Dwyer, Chief Executive Officer of NexTel Medical Corp. "The overwhelming interest from industry partners reinforces our confidence in our technology pipeline. We are already scheduling follow-up discussions regarding strategic vendor collaborations, while actively refining our educational outreach to accelerate clinical adoption."

As a result of the enthusiastic reception from industry stakeholders, NexTel leadership is scheduled to conduct follow-up commercialization and partnership discussions with several prominent vendors next week.

About NexTel Medical Corp.

NexTel Medical Corp. is a pioneering biotechnology leader at the forefront of exosome research, clinical diagnostics, and wellness accessibility. The Company specializes in developing proprietary, next-generation, exosome-based delivery systems and non-invasive screening tools designed to revolutionize both therapeutic and diagnostic modalities.

NexTel's fully integrated ecosystem spans four core strategic divisions, bridging the gap between complex biotech innovation and scalable market delivery:

  • Maxasome Health Check: Proprietary non-invasive liquid biopsy diagnostics utilizing the NANOG DNA assay for universal early-stage cancer screening.
  • Maxasome™ PLUS: Next-generation, high-bioavailability wellness therapeutics powered by 100% pure exosomal delivery systems.

data.title: Buyback plans are slowing but 2026 may still be a record
data.description:
Key points:
  • Main US indexes advance; Dow out front, up ~0.8%
  • Tech leads S&P 500 sector gainers; energy is weakest group
  • Dollar, bitcoin dip; US crude down >2.5%; gold up slightly
  • US 10-year Treasury yield rises to ~5.20%

BUYBACK PLANS ARE SLOWING BUT 2026 MAY STILL BE A RECORD

In a choppy year for share buybacks, EPFR is reporting "exceptionally light" announcements so far in September.

After announcements of buyback authorizations adding up to $973.7 billion in the first six months of the year, EPFR analyst Winston Chua notes that momentum has "reversed sharply" since mid-year.

From July through September 23, buyback announcements of $196.4 billion compared with $368.5 billion in the same timeframe a year ago, marking a decline of roughly 50%.

And with just a week left in September at the time of his tally, announcements had totaled $20 billion compared with the $67 billion total for September in 2025 and the 10-year September average of $61.5 billion, according to the data from EPFR, a unit of ISI Markets.

The slowdown comes after the $133.8 billion announced in August and $42.8 billion in July.

"If this month’s figures fall below $25 billion, it will mark the second-lowest September volume in 15 years," according to Chua, but he wrote that the slowdown appeared to reflect "a lack of large programs rather than a broad-based retreat from buybacks."

But even with the recent slowdown, he wrote that a strong first half of 2026 means that a full-year record is still within reach.

"Roughly $250 billion of additional announcements would still surpass 2025’s $1.39 trillion total," he wrote, noting that in the last five years fourth-quarter buybacks averaged $271 billion.
